items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A fixed finite population \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(n\ge4\) and a degree index \(1\le d\le n-1\). A schedule \(\theta=(G,a,t,b)\) consists of a simple directed off-diagonal graph \(G\) on \(V\) (an arrow \((j,i)\) points from treatment source \(j\) to outcome recipient \(i\)) and real coefficients. Potential outcomes are additive, \(Y_i(z)=a_i+t_iz_i+\sum_{j:(j,i)\in G}b_{ij}z_j\) for \(z\in\{0,1\}^V\), and the causal target is \(\tau(\theta)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V}[Y_i(\mathbf1)-Y_i(\mathbf0)]\). The class \(\mathcal M_{n,d}\) collects the schedules with in-degree and out-degree at most \(d\) and coefficient mass \(|a_i|+|t_i|+\sum_{j:(j,i)\in G}|b_{ij}|\le1\) for every \(i\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: One experiment on the fixed schedule: the assignment \(Z\in\{0,1\}^V\) has independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) coordinates; independently, each ordered off-diagonal pair carries an audit mark \(W_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\) with known \(q\in[0,1]\). The recorded graph is \(H=\{(j,i)\in G:W_{ij}=1\}\), the centered signs are \(X_j=2Z_j-1\), and the full record is \(O=(H,Z,Y(Z))\) with every edge label, treatment coordinate and noiseless outcome. An independent uniform seed \(\xi\in[0,1]\) represents estimator randomization, and \(P_{\theta,q}\) is the law of \((O,\xi)\) with \(\theta\) fixed.

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl:
\[
\mathcal M_{n,d}=
\left\{\theta=(G,a,t,b):
\max_{i\in V}|\{j:(j,i)\in G\}|\le d,\ 
\max_{j\in V}|\{i:(j,i)\in G\}|\le d,\ 
\max_{i\in V}\left(|a_i|+|t_i|+\sum_{j:(j,i)\in G}|b_{ij}|\right)\le1
\right\},
\]
for \(n\ge4\) and \(1\le d\le n-1\), with \(G\) directed, simple, and off-diagonal. The schedule notation is the published SNIPE \(\beta=1\) coefficient-mass model \cite{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023SNIPE}, restricted to compulsory diagonal coordinates after augmentation. The corresponding published total in-degree and out-degree bound is \(d+1\); \(d\) here counts only off-diagonal arrows. The own coordinate is always available and is not thinned. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:published-model}\) proves the faithful specialization and reindexing. The off-diagonal audit is the observation channel specified separately in the design assumptions.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(R_{n,d}(q)=\inf_T\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}\mathcal L(T;\theta,q)\), with \(\mathcal L(T;\theta,q)=\mathbb E_{P_{\theta,q}}[(T(O,\xi)-\tau(\theta))^2]\) and \(\xi\) independent uniform on \([0,1]\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: For \(2m\le n\), draw \(S\) uniformly over its ordered source partitions and draw \(U_1,\ldots,U_B\) independently with density \(f\), independently of \(S\). The graph contains all \((j,i)\) with \(j\in S_\ell\) and \(i\in C_\ell\). Set \(a_i=U_\ell-\sigma h/2\), \(t_i=0\), and \(b_{ij}=\sigma h/d\) on these arrows for \(i\in C_\ell\). All source and padding outcomes are zero. The resulting distribution over fixed \(\theta\) is \(\Pi_{\sigma,h}\); \(P_{\sigma,h}\) is its original-record mixture. Baselines are drawn before randomization and are not measurement noise.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl:
The precision handle names the explicit scale--rule pair \((F,T^\star_{n,d,q})\) of Definitions \(\mathrm{def:frontier-scale}\) and \(\mathrm{def:frontier-rule}\):
\[
F(n,d,q)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{1,d^2/(n[1-(1-q)^d])\},&q>0,\\
1,&q=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
T^\star_{n,d,q}(O)=
\begin{cases}
\max\{-1,\min\{1,T_q(O)\}\},&q>0,\ u(n,d,q)<1,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Its positive-retention elbow expression is \(\min\{1,d^2/n+d/(nq)\}\). Its sequence criteria are \(d_n^2/n\to0\) and \(d_n/(nq_n)\to0\), assigning \(+\infty\) to the second ratio at zero retention. The uniform risk comparison, equivalence of the elbow expression, and necessity and sufficiency of those criteria are proved in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:observed-record-precision-frontier}\); they are not membership conditions or conclusions inserted by definition. The original-record converse is supplied by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:block-testing-scale}\), using the complete conditional likelihood of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:block-law}\), and retains \(H,Z,Y(Z)\) and the global treated-source count \(K\).

items.label: Definition P-9
Definition P-10
items.nl:
For \(n\ge4\), \(1\le d\le n-1\), and \(q\in[0,1]\), define
\[
F(n,d,q)=\begin{cases}
\min\left\{1,\dfrac{d^2}{n[1-(1-q)^d]}\right\},&q>0,\\
1,&q=0.
\end{cases}
\]
This is a positive finite function; the relation to minimax risk is a theorem, not part of this definition.

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl: For every admissible \(n,d,q\), define \(T^\star_{n,d,q}(O)=T^{\mathrm{up}}(O)\), with \(T^{\mathrm{up}}\) exactly as in Definition \(\mathrm{def:upper-rule}\). In particular it is zero when \(q=0\) or \(u(n,d,q)\ge1\), and otherwise clips the observable \(T_q\) to \([-1,1]\).

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl:
For fixed admissible \(n,d,q\), define the supplied-graph minimax risk by
\[
R^G_{n,d}(q)=\inf_{T^G}\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\theta,q}}\!\left[
  \bigl(T^G(O,G(\theta),\xi)-\tau(\theta)\bigr)^2
\right].
\]
Here \(G(\theta)\) denotes the true off-diagonal graph component of the fixed schedule \(\theta\). The infimum ranges over all Borel-measurable functions
\[
T^G:\operatorname{range}(O)\times
2^{\{(j,i)\in V^2:j\ne i\}}\times[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathbb R.
\]
The finite graph coordinate has the discrete sigma-algebra, and the original record has the Borel sigma-algebra inherited from its finite graph and assignment coordinates and real outcome coordinates. The estimator may use the known \(n,d,q\). The law \(P_{\theta,q}\), schedule class, causal target, and independent uniform seed are exactly those of Definition \(\mathrm{def:risk}\); the additional observation is solely \(G(\theta)\). Expectations of the nonnegative loss are interpreted in \([0,+\infty]\), so no integrability restriction is imposed on an estimator.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}\) and \(q>0\), \(\mathbb E_{P_{\theta,q}}T_q=\tau(\theta)\) and \[\operatorname{Var}_{P_{\theta,q}}(T_q)=\operatorname{Var}_{Z}(T_G)+\frac{4(1-q)}{n^2q}\sum_{i\in V}|\{j:(j,i)\in G\}|\,\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)^2].\] Also \(\operatorname{Var}_{Z}(T_G)\le5(d+1)^2/n\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For \(2m\le n\), \(\Pi_{\sigma,h}(\mathcal M_{n,d})=1\) and \(\tau(\theta)=\sigma mh/n\) on its support. Each source association is independently revealed with probability \(p\). For every \((H,Z)\) having positive probability, \[\lambda_{\sigma,h}(y\mid H,Z)=\frac{[x^K]\prod_{\ell=1}^B\left\{\sum_{k=0}^{u_\ell}\binom{u_\ell}{k}f\!\left(y_\ell-\frac{\sigma h(A_\ell+2k-u_\ell)}{2d}\right)x^k\right\}}{\binom{M}{K}}.\] At \(M=0\), \(K=0\) and \(\binom00=1\). The law of \(O\) is recovered from the actual joint marginal of \((H,Z)\) and this conditional density by copying \(y_\ell\) to all recipients in \(C_\ell\) and assigning zero to source and padding outcomes. Detailed retained-edge subsets, full source labels, and all treatment coordinates are included in that joint marginal.

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
For the declared density \(f\), put \(\varphi=\sqrt f\). Then \(\varphi\) is globally \(4\pi\)-Lipschitz and \(\int\varphi'(w)^2\,dw=4\pi^2\). For any real shifts \(s,t\),
\[
\int\left(\sqrt{f(w-s)}-\sqrt{f(w-t)}\right)^2dw\le4\pi^2(s-t)^2.
\]
For product translated densities, the squared Hellinger distance, defined as the integral of the squared difference of square roots, is at most the sum of these one-coordinate bounds. Total variation is at most the square root of this squared Hellinger distance. The same product bound may be averaged over a common observed marginal.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
Let \(d\ge1\) and \(0\le h\le1/4\). For \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^d\), define
\[
F_\varepsilon(w)=f\!\left(w-\frac{h}{2d}\sum_{j=1}^d\varepsilon_j\right),
\qquad g_d(w)=2^{-d}\sum_\varepsilon F_\varepsilon(w).
\]
On \(g_d>0\), expand the likelihood in signs as
\[
\frac{F_\varepsilon(w)}{g_d(w)}=
\sum_{E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}a_{|E|}(w)\prod_{j\in E}\varepsilon_j,
\qquad a_0=1.
\]
The coefficients exist by finite Walsh expansion and depend only on \(|E|\). Set \(\gamma_s=\int a_s(w)^2g_d(w)\,dw\) for \(1\le s\le d\), and
\[
\eta=\sum_{s=1}^d\binom ds\gamma_s,
\qquad \eta_1=\sum_{s=1}^d s\binom ds\gamma_s.
\]
Then \(\int a_sg_d=0\) for \(s\ge1\), and
\[
0\le\eta\le\eta_1\le\frac{12\pi^2h^2}{d}.
\]
Values of the coefficients on \(g_d=0\) do not affect these integrals.

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
Assume \(2m=2Bd\le n\) and use the complete block experiment of Definition \(\mathrm{def:block-prior}\). Use \(g_d,\gamma_s,\eta,\eta_1\) from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:walsh-channel-energy}\). Conditional on the complete retained graph \(H\), let \(Q_H\) have the actual assignment marginal and independent distinct responses with density \(g_d\); let \(L_+\) be the density ratio of \(P_{+1,h}(Z,y\mid H)\) to \(Q_H\). Write \(\chi_H^2=\mathbb E_{Q_H}(L_+-1)^2\). If \(4e\eta<1\), then
\[
\mathbb E_H\!\left[\mathbf1\{M\ge m/4\}\chi_H^2\right]
\le\frac{\exp(eBp\eta_1)}{1-4e\eta}-1.
\]
The expectation uses the actual retained-edge marginal, including its labels and detailed edge subsets.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
Fix admissible \(n,d,q\). Let two priors on \(\mathcal M_{n,d}\) be supported on schedules with respective constant causal targets \(+\Delta\) and \(-\Delta\), where \(\Delta>0\). Let \(\mathsf Q_+,\mathsf Q_-\) be their full \(O\) mixture laws. Then
\[
R_{n,d}(q)\ge\frac{\Delta^2}{2}
\left(1-\operatorname{TV}(\mathsf Q_+,\mathsf Q_-)\right).
\]
This bound applies to every measurable randomized \(T(O,\xi)\).

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For every admissible \(n,d,q\),
\[
R_{n,d}(q)\ge\frac1{160000\pi^2}
\min\left\{1,\frac{(d+1)^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
This is a lower bound for arbitrary measurable randomized functions of the complete original record. In addition, the supplied-graph minimax risk of Definition \(\mathrm{def:supplied-risk}\) satisfies the identical bound:
\[
R^G_{n,d}(q)\ge\frac1{160000\pi^2}
\min\left\{1,\frac{(d+1)^2}{n}\right\}.
\]
The second assertion allows every Borel-measurable randomized estimator of the complete original record together with the true off-diagonal graph.

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
For \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}\), adjoin all diagonal arrows and write
\[
\widetilde G=G\cup\{(i,i):i\in V\},\qquad
c^{\mathrm{pub}}_{i,\varnothing}=a_i,\quad
c^{\mathrm{pub}}_{i,\{i\}}=t_i,\quad
c^{\mathrm{pub}}_{i,\{j\}}=b_{ij}\quad((j,i)\in G),
\]
with all remaining polynomial coefficients zero. This is a published SNIPE schedule with interaction order \(\beta=1\), coefficient-mass bound \(Y_{\max}\le1\), and total in-degree and out-degree at most \(d+1\), restricted to graphs containing every diagonal arrow. Removing those diagonal arrows is the inverse correspondence. The correspondence preserves every \(Y_i(z)\) and the causal total treatment effect \(\tau(\theta)\). It is a faithful specialization and degree reindexing of the published model, rather than equality with its class at the same degree index \(d\). When the same independent half-Bernoulli assignment and off-diagonal thinning channel are used, adjoining known diagonal arrows also gives an invertible deterministic transformation of \(O\). Therefore a minimax lower bound on \(\mathcal M_{n,d}\) transfers to any containing published schedule class under that same observation channel by class inclusion.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For all \(n\ge4\), \(1\le d\le n-1\), and \(q\in[0,1]\), \[R_{n,d}(q)\le\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}\mathcal L(T^{\mathrm{up}};\theta,q)\le\min\{1,u(n,d,q)\}.\] The rule \(T^{\mathrm{up}}\) is finite and measurable for every possible observed \(O\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
There are universal \(c,C_0>0\) such that, for every admissible \(n,d,q\),
\[
R_{n,d}(q)\ge c\max\left\{\min\{1,(d+1)^2/n\},\frac1{1+nq}\right\}.
\]
In particular, \(c\le R_{n,d}(0)\le1\), \(c\min\{1,(d+1)^2/n\}\le R_{n,d}(1)\le C_0\min\{1,(d+1)^2/n\}\), and \(c/(1+nq)\le R_{n,1}(q)\le C_0/(1+nq)\). Every lower bound is for all measurable randomized estimators of the full \(O\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
For every \(B,d\ge1\), \(2Bd\le n\), and \(q\in[0,1]\), put \(m=Bd\), \(p=1-(1-q)^d\), and
\[
s(B,d,q)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,d/\sqrt{mp}\},&p>0,\\1,&p=0.\end{cases}
\qquad \kappa=\frac1{100\pi}.
\]
For the complete original-record mixture laws of Definition \(\mathrm{def:block-prior}\),
\[
0\le h\le\kappa s(B,d,q)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1,h},P_{-1,h})\le\frac12.
\]
For \(h>0,p>0\) their distance also satisfies
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1,h},P_{-1,h})
\ge1-\frac{7d^2}{8h^2mp}.
\]
Thus, if \(\bar h(B,d,q)=\sup\{h\in[0,1/4]:\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1,h},P_{-1,h})\le1/2\}\), then
\[
\kappa s(B,d,q)\le\bar h(B,d,q)\le2s(B,d,q).
\]
In particular the largest permissible order is \(\min\{1,d/\sqrt{Bd[1-(1-q)^d]}\}\), with value one when \(q=0\), uniformly in block count and degree.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
Let \(F\) and \(T^\star_{n,d,q}\) be the explicit scale and total rule in Definitions \(\mathrm{def:frontier-scale}\) and \(\mathrm{def:frontier-rule}\):
\[
F(n,d,q)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,d^2/(n[1-(1-q)^d])\},&q>0,\\1,&q=0,\end{cases}
\qquad T^\star_{n,d,q}=T^{\mathrm{up}}.
\]
There are universal \(c,C_0>0\) such that, simultaneously for every \(n\ge4\), \(1\le d\le n-1\), and \(q\in[0,1]\),
\[
cF(n,d,q)\le R_{n,d}(q)
\le\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}\mathcal L(T^\star_{n,d,q};\theta,q)
\le C_0F(n,d,q).
\]
The lower bound includes every measurable randomized estimator of the complete \(O\), and the upper rule uses only \(O,n,d,q\). For any admissible sequences \(d_n,q_n\), a sequence of total observable estimators with worst-case mean squared error tending to zero exists if and only if
\[
\frac{d_n^2}{n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
\frac{d_n}{nq_n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the second ratio is \(+\infty\) at \(q_n=0\). In particular \(F(n,d,0)=1\), \(F(n,d,1)=\min\{1,d^2/n\}\), and for positive retention the scale is, up to universal constants, \(\min\{1,d^2/n+d/(nq)\}\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
For positive integers \(B,d\) with \(2Bd\le n\), put \(m=Bd\), \(p=1-(1-q)^d\), and
\[
s=\begin{cases}\min\{1,d/\sqrt{mp}\},&p>0,\\1,&p=0.\end{cases}
\]
For the complete original-record block laws, the radius
\[
\bar h=\sup\{h\in[0,1/4]:\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1,h},P_{-1,h})\le1/2\}
\]
satisfies \((100\pi)^{-1}s\le\bar h\le2s\). Moreover every \(0\le h\le(100\pi)^{-1}s\) has distance at most \(1/2\). In degree two this scale is \(\min\{1,\sqrt{2/[B(2q-q^2)]}\}\) for \(q>0\), and one at \(q=0\), uniformly over every block count. Thus this family itself supplies the uniform all-degree original-record testing bound; no replacement prior or deletion of observed graph or outcome information is required.

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
For all \(n\ge4\), \(1\le d\le n-1\), and \(q\in[0,1]\), the explicit scale and total observable rule of Definitions \(\mathrm{def:frontier-scale}\) and \(\mathrm{def:frontier-rule}\) satisfy
\[
\frac{F(n,d,q)}{2560000\pi^2}
\le R_{n,d}(q)
\le\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}\mathcal L(T^\star_{n,d,q};\theta,q)
\le24F(n,d,q),
\qquad
F(n,d,q)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,d^2/[n(1-(1-q)^d)]\},&q>0,\\1,&q=0.\end{cases}
\]
Here \(T^\star=T^{\mathrm{up}}\), using only \(O,n,d,q\). Uniform consistency along arbitrary admissible \(d_n,q_n\) is possible exactly when \(d_n^2/n\to0\) and \(d_n/(nq_n)\to0\), with the second ratio \(+\infty\) at \(q_n=0\). At positive retention the scale is equivalent, with universal constants, to \(\min\{1,d^2/n+d/(nq)\}\); at full retention it is \(\min\{1,d^2/n\}\). The converse covers every measurable randomized estimator of the entire \(O\).

items.label: Cited result lem:snipe-model-conventions
items.nl: The SNIPE fixed-schedule model uses a directed graph whose in-neighborhoods may contain their own vertices. Its interaction-order-one outcome polynomial consists of a constant term and singleton-coordinate terms in each in-neighborhood. The coefficient-mass envelope is the maximum, over vertices, of the sum of the absolute values of these polynomial coefficients, including the constant coefficient. The coefficient restrictions do not require a nonzero singleton coefficient for each graph edge. These are the model conventions in Sections 3.1--3.2, Assumptions 1--2 and equations (3.2)--(3.3) of \cite{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023SNIPE}.
